clue.text: How's that possibly a parish's first set of 20?

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word parish is taken

parts.note: 20-down is CHANGES, and a peal is a full set of changes rung on bells

explanation.surface: A cricket appeal mixed up with a village church's first round of bell-ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's that?' is the cricket fielder's appeal to the umpire. A, then P (first of 'parish'), then PEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, 'How's that?' (howzat) is the call players make when asking the umpire for a wicket, which is called an appeal.

clue.text: Set of 20 in flat — result of scout doing two more jobs?

parts.note: flat means plain, as in a plain or level surface
in bob-a-job week a scout did a job and earned a bob, an old shilling
one job plus two more makes it triple, so the earnings are trebled

explanation.surface: A scout doing odd jobs in a flat for his bob-a-job earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob-a-job was a British Scout fundraising week in which each small job earned a 'bob', slang for a shilling coin. Plain Bob Triples is a bell-ringing method on seven bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain Bob Triples is a named method of change ringing, a way of ringing a set of changes on bells.

clue.text: Key copies for jailbreaks, say

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: Duplicating keys so prisoners can break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'copies' read together as a key-cutting job, but they are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailbreak is one example of an escape from custody, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Your starter: one snail, freshly cooked with onions

indicators.note: cooking afresh means the letters are reworked into a new dish
the starter of a word is its opening letter, here of Your

explanation.surface: A menu offering you a starter of a single snail cooked with onions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly cooked' shuffles Y (the starter of 'Your') with ONESNAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyonnaise is a cooking term for dishes prepared in the style of Lyons, with sliced fried onions.

clue.text: Launches takeaway illegally, so gets fines

parts.note: to lift something is to steal it, taking it away illegally
F is the abbreviation for fine (as on pencils), doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone stealing a takeaway meal and being fined for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takeaway' looks like a meal, but it is the verb 'take away': stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket that launches lifts off the ground, the two verbs meaning the same.

clue.text: Upstanding person, Italian, housing Mexicans in New Mexico?

indicators.note: Upstanding says the hidden letters are read backwards, upwards in a down light
housing means the words contain the answer's letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An upright Italian who gives a home to Mexican people living in New Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'housing' in the definition, but it is the hidden-word indicator; the definition is 'Mexicans in New Mexico?'.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Latin American descent in the US are called Latinos, and Mexicans in New Mexico are one example.

clue.text: See 8
One allegedly met after death of first pet, Ermintrude

indicators.note: of here means the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Mourning a first pet, a cow called Ermintrude.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermintrude is the cow in the children's show The Magic Roundabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition holds that Saint Peter keeps the gates of heaven and greets the dead there.

clue.text: Vegetarian starter mix, all oddly used for number of 20 in 7 9 17's celebrated 2

definitions.text: Vegetarian starter mix, all oddly used for number of 20 in 7 9 17's celebrated 2

parts.words: Vegetarian starter mix, all oddly used for number of 20 in 7 9 17's celebrated 2
parts.note: V (start of Vegetarian), then M, X, L (odd letters of mix and all) as Roman numerals give 5 thousand 40, the number of changes in the famous peal at St Peter Mancroft, Norwich

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a vegetarian starter that turns into bell-ringing history.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters V, M, XL are not entered: read as Roman numerals they say five, thousand, forty. The first true peal, Plain Bob Triples, was rung at St Peter Mancroft in Norwich in 1715.
explanation.definitionFit: A full peal on seven bells is all possible orderings, seven factorial, a total of 5040 changes.

clue.text: Working farm not occupied by Cornwall's first Conservative peer

indicators.note: occupied by means a letter sits inside the rearranged letters
working means the letters are put to work in a new order
first means just the opening letter of the word Cornwall

explanation.surface: A Cornish farm that the first Tory peer never lived in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' shuffles FARMNOT into MANROFT; 'occupied by' puts C (first of 'Cornwall's') inside it. Lord Mancroft was a Conservative politician in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Baron Mancroft is a title held in the House of Lords, and its holders sat as Conservatives.

clue.text: Traveller greeting flag again

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller
ave is the Latin word of greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A traveller waving a flag in greeting once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is the paving stone (flagstone), not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag a path is to lay flagstones on it, so flagging it again means laying a new surface.

clue.text: Article used in party game

indicators.note: used in means a letter is placed inside another word

parts.note: SNP is the Scottish National Party
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An object needed for a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party game' reads as one phrase, but 'party' is SNP and 'game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a simple card game in which players race to call out when two matching cards appear.

clue.text: How Singapore is described by some kid's mother, say

definitions.text: How Singapore is described by some

parts.note: a kid is a young goat, and its mother is a nanny goat
to say is to state

explanation.surface: A child's mother describing Singapore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' is a young goat, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore's strict, paternalistic rules have led critics to call it a government that over-protects and interferes like a nursemaid.

clue.text: Sloth shown by partners after trimming box tree

indicators.note: after means the pieces before it come later in the answer than the trimmed box
trimming the word box cuts off its last letter

parts.note: N and S are partners in bridge, North and South
the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: Slothful partners cutting a box hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box tree' looks like the definition, but 'box' is trimmed to BO and 'tree' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature tree kept small by pruning in a pot.

clue.text: Abandoned Romeo after girl? Lots here, perhaps

indicators.note: after means the rearranged Romeo follows the girl

parts.note: Sal is a short girl's name, from Sally

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A jilted Romeo trailing after a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' shuffles ROMEO into EROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are items put up for auction, and an auction room is where they are sold.

clue.text: Queen's favourite city

definitions.meaning: Robert Dudley, Earl of that title, was the favourite of Elizabeth I
a city in the English East Midlands

explanation.surface: The Queen's favourite city.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley was made earl of this name and was Elizabeth I's favourite; it is also an English city.

clue.text: Most impoverished characters in Boston, ie students

indicators.note: characters in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The poorest residents of Boston are its students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most impoverished' uses the British idiom 'stony broke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stony, short for stony broke, means having no money at all.

clue.text: City choir now disheartened, sadly

indicators.note: sadly means the letters come out in a sorry, disordered state
disheartened means the middle letter of now is removed

explanation.surface: A city's choir is now dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves NW from 'now'; 'sadly' shuffles CHOIR plus NW.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is a cathedral city in Norfolk, in the east of England.

clue.text: Getting 6 in test's not worth mentioning

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a trial is a test
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Scoring six in a test match, hardly worth a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the light 6-down, but here it is simply the number, VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is so slight or unimportant that it isn't worth bringing up.

clue.text: Packed as a precautionary provision

definitions.meaning: put away inside a box or holder
to be ready should something happen

explanation.definitionFit: Literally 'inside a box' for packed, and the idiom meaning just as a precaution.

clue.text: Puts clean nappy on small child by river leaving French city

parts.note: ch is the abbreviation for child

indicators.note: leaving means the letter goes out of the city's name

parts.note: Angers is a city in western France

explanation.surface: Changing a toddler's nappy beside a river after leaving a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: A nappy is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a fresh diaper on a baby is called changing it.

clue.text: Ex-PM's 50% vituperation, 50% outrageously obstreperous

indicators.note: 50% of the statesman's name means keeping only its first half

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian prime minister

indicators.note: outrageously means the letters are thrown into wild disorder
50% of vituperation means its first six letters only

explanation.surface: Half of a former prime minister's output is abuse, half outrageous rowdiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 50% cuts DISRAELI to DISR; the second keeps VITUPE, which 'outrageously' shuffles into UPTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstreperous behaviour is noisy and unruly, causing disturbance, a close synonym.

clue.text: Series of 20 after moving left up to daughter to offer in excuse

indicators.note: moving signals that one letter shifts its position in the word
up, in a down clue, says the letter goes higher, towards the start

parts.note: 20-down is CHANGES, and a peal is a series of changes rung on bells

explanation.surface: Moving left up to one's daughter, offering a series of excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving L up in PEAL gives PLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead something is to put it forward as an excuse, as in pleading ignorance.

clue.text: Spots gas bill first

indicators.note: first means the bill comes ahead of the gas

parts.note: ac is the abbreviation for account, a bill
Ne is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: Seeing the gas bill first.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, which are commonly called spots.

clue.text: Girl writing paper in college

indicators.note: in means the paper goes inside the college

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University
the i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A girl writing a college paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing paper' suggests stationery, but the paper is the i, a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Claire is a common female given name.

clue.text: Playing triangle for function

indicators.note: playing means the letters are played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Playing the triangle at a function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like an event, but it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In calculus an integral is a function obtained by integration, the antiderivative.

clue.text: One blooming peal's wrong, including flipping first note

indicators.note: including means one piece is held inside the other
wrong means the letters are set out wrongly
flipping means the note's name is turned back to front

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bell peal that has gone wrong, with someone saying 'flipping' at the first note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, but it signals the reversal; 'wrong' and 'including' then wrap the shuffled peal's letters around the turned note.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a flowering plant of the lily family, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Sit in chair, topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to chair a meeting is to preside over it

explanation.surface: Sitting in a chair without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' is a verb, to preside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to sit in a formal sense, as a court or a power is said to sit or be vested somewhere.
